title: Collecting Sound Words
description: For ages 6–9 with an adult: listen for buzz, splash, and pop, and collect words that sound just like their sounds.

body.heading: Listen first
paragraphs: Sit somewhere quiet with your adult. What can you hear? A clock might tick. A tap might drip.
Say each sound slowly. Some words copy the sound they name, like buzz, splash, pop, and hush.

body.heading: Start your collection
paragraphs: Draw or write each sound word you find on your page. Add a tiny picture of what made the sound.
By the end of the day, you might have a whole page of words that you can almost hear.

takeaway: Some words sound like the noises they name, and collecting them is like collecting treasures.
safetyNotes: Listen quietly and stay close to your adult, indoors or outdoors.
screenFreeExtension: Close your eyes for one minute and count how many different sounds you can hear.
